title: Central-to-satellite native relay wakes are never admitted: the satellite records central as enrolled, and wake admission requires an active home peer
outcome: A routine mail that a central-host session sends to a remote-root proxy (the native relay route) wakes the satellite's native target session, in the real deployment where only central has activated the pair. A wake that cannot be admitted is visible on the home side, not retried forever without trace.
acceptance: A two-host regression with the real topology (the satellite records central as enrolled, only central activates) delivers a central-homed relay wake to the satellite's native root as a queued turn; it is RED on master before the fix

Revocation, a changed enrollment, quarantine, a replaced target and link loss still hold the wake; the existing relay_review tests stay green, except that the one relay_review_r2 reconnect assertion that encoded this defect (holding the wake after a reconnect until the satellite side was re-activated) is changed to expect the re-drive on the fresh lease, disclosed on the item and reviewed explicitly by the pair
A refused home wake is observable: a bounded log line and a read-only diagnostic, metadata only, with the obligation's last refusal and attempt count; plus a test
docs/features/native-mailbox-relay.md states which side's membership gates wake admission

completion.summary: Historical delivered work reconciled; 6365481c; real enrolled-central topology tests/refusal diagnostics + FULL9239386b; a4266e7a records later actual satellite wakes. Closure/evidence mapping, not new admission code.
